evidence_rows.lay_context: Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) are important protein complexes, and their substrate receptor subunits must be carefully regulated to ensure the cell has a complete set of these ligases.
allowed_evidence_spans: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases ( CRLs ) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs .
It is thus critical to regulate F-box protein levels .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Unbalanced levels can lead to sequestration of CRL core components by a few overabundant substrate receptors.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Unbalanced levels of substrate receptor subunits can lead to sequestration of CRL core components by a few overabundant substrate receptors.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Depending on the cell type , hundreds of different F-box proteins can compete for the single binding site on the common SCF core complex .
evidence_rows.lay_context: If the levels of these receptor subunits are not balanced, a few too-abundant receptors can bind and tie up the core components of CRLs, preventing other ligases from forming.
allowed_evidence_spans: Unbalanced levels can lead to sequestration of CRL core components by a few overabundant substrate receptors .

Accordingly , over expression of a single F-box protein in yeast can change the balanced distribution and diversity of available SCF complexes by sequestering cullin and Skp1 and thus block formation of functional SCF complexes with other F-box proteins [10 , 11 , 14] .

evidence_rows.lay_context: Problems with the regulation of these receptor components, especially in SCF ligases (the largest group of CRLs), have been linked to many diseases, including cancer.
allowed_evidence_spans: Numerous diseases , including cancer , have been associated with misregulation of substrate receptor components , particularly for the largest class of CRLs , the SCF ligases .

evidence_rows.lay_context: One known way the cell controls the amount of F-box proteins (which are substrate receptors for SCF ligases) is through a process where the complete SCF complex tags the F-box protein with ubiquitin, leading to its breakdown by the proteasome.

evidence_rows.core_keep_af: This study describes an additional pathway for regulating F-box proteins, using yeast Met30 as an example.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Studying the yeast F-box protein Met30 as a model , we have uncovered a novel mechanism for degradation of F-box proteins .
evidence_rows.lay_context: This study identifies a new way that F-box proteins are regulated, using the yeast protein Met30 as a model to understand this process.
allowed_evidence_spans: Here we describe an additional pathway for regulation of F-box proteins on the example of yeast Met30 .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: This ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: This newly described ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This pathway targets free F-box proteins and requires part of the SCF core .
evidence_rows.lay_context: This new pathway specifically targets Met30 proteins that are not bound to Skp1, leading to their ubiquitylation and subsequent degradation.
allowed_evidence_spans: This ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1 .

These results suggest a proteolytic pathway that recognizes unbound ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 to avoid accumulation of excess unbound Met30 , which could bind substrates and shield them from recognition by fully assembled SCFMet30 complexes .

Thus , these results provide evidence for existence of an additional , Skp1-independent , degradation pathway for several F-box proteins , which appears to target F-box proteins that are not bound to the SCF core complex.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Unexpectedly, this pathway required the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but was independent of the other central SCF component Skp1.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The newly described pathway unexpectedly requires the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but is independent of the other central SCF component Skp1.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This pathway targets free F-box proteins and requires part of the SCF core .
evidence_rows.lay_context: Surprisingly, this degradation pathway needs the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1, but it does not need Skp1, which is another key component of the SCF complex.
allowed_evidence_spans: Unexpectedly , this pathway required the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but was independent of the other central SCF component Skp1 .

Importantly , this ubiquitylation pathway does not require Skp1 ( Skp1-independent Cul1-dependent ubiquitylation ) and suggests a function of Cdc53/Cul1 that is independent from association with Skp1 .

As previously observed , unbound Met30 was rapidly degraded in skp1-25 mutants but , importantly , was stabilized upon inactivation of cdc53-1 in the double mutant ( Fig 2C ) , confirming that degradation was dependent on Cdc53 but not Skp1 .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We demonstrated that this non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: This non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress in yeast.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study showed that this unusual degradation pathway is essential for maintaining stable chromosomes and for the cell's ability to protect itself from heavy metal stress.
allowed_evidence_spans: We demonstrated that this non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress .
We reasoned that the Skp1-independent degradation pathway should be particularly important for the recovery from heavy metal stress.
In addition to enhanced cadmium sensitivity , Met30M178E/I179E mutants displayed increased chromosome loss ( Fig 8E ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: More importantly, our results assign important biological functions to a sub-complex of cullin-RING ligases that comprises Cdc53/Rbx1/Cdc34, but is independent of Skp1.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The results assign important biological functions to a sub-complex of cullin-RING ligases comprising Cdc53/Rbx1/Cdc34, which is independent of Skp1.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: These findings add an additional layer to our understanding of regulation of multisubunit E3 ligase .
evidence_rows.lay_context: These findings highlight significant biological roles for a specific sub-complex of cullin-RING ligases, made up of Cdc53, Rbx1, and Cdc34, that operates without Skp1.
allowed_evidence_spans: More importantly , our results assign important biological functions to a sub-complex of cullin-RING ligases that comprises Cdc53/Rbx1/Cdc34 , but is independent of Skp1 .
This degradation pathway targets Met30 that is detached from Skp1 and involves the SCF core components Cdc53 and Rbx1 , as well as the cognate SCF ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 .
Together , our findings shed light on the regulation and complexity of E3 ligases and suggest additional diversity in the cullin-RING family of ubiquitin ligases .
